The task board is the doctrine's worked example because every hard part of a two-level split already exists and is already good — snapshot cache, live spine, forward-only merge, honest connection states, rev-CAS writes, a replay-safe event feed. Only the wire is monolithic: every paint pulls 9.14 MB of full-depth JSON to draw rows that need 0.4 MB. This paper freezes the split end to end — board tier, focused tier, cache-by-rev, live invalidation, failure honesty — and distills the four-piece kit every other Barkpark surface inherits. The thesis
The split is a WIRE-TIER swap inside an architecture already split everywhere else. Board tier rides a manifest-declared task view (measured 22.5–27× lighter, live on guerrilla today as ?view=brief); focused tier rides task.get (14,048 B live), fetched on focus and prefetched; details are cached content-addressed by (doc_id, rev) with TTL infinite — rev is already the system's CAS token; the binding id→current-rev moves over the replay-safe /v1/tasks/events keyset feed, which is built, live-verified, and consumed by ZERO Go code today. The iron rule survives amended: events never carry truth — they carry ADDRESSES. And the diet does more than save bytes: the corpus is 3,118 tasks but the list clamps at 1,000 — the split un-truncates the board.

What we will create

Two wire tiers replacing one monolith. Nothing else in the architecture moves: the first-paint snapshot cache, the ●/◐/✗ honesty vocabulary, mergeForward, flash-diff, and the debounced live loop all survive.

The board-tier card — frozen field by field

The external reviewer's 'compact truth' was overweight: criteria text, why-prose, and endgame do not ride the board — meaning is one retrieve away. But the AXI brief card v2 is too light: an empirical field→consumer census (every read site in internal/taskboard/*.go + internal/cli/*.go, tagged board-paint / wide-preview / detail-frame / paper-rail / CLI) proves the board paints eight things brief v2 cut.   • Everything the split needs already exists, unassembled. The /v1/tasks/events feed carries {id, event, doc_id, rev, at} with a replay-safe cursor — and has ZERO Go consumers. The design renegotiates frozen contracts — say so, never slip it

The epic charter must open with explicit unfreezing language and the evidence that earned it (9.14 MB, 32% truncation). A build wave that quietly contradicts them repeats the false-done class of failure.
  • Drift honesty debt: today's board is drift-free by construction (refetch everything). Each cache layer added must prove its own honesty — badge visible, cursor validated, out-of-order fenced — as acceptance criteria with mutation-proven tests, not vibes.
  • Merge hazard if board rides brief unmodified: the seconds/claim cuts are not cosmetic; shipping the board on brief v2 as-is can strand stale claimed rows. Block on the card fix, not on hope.
  • Fail-closed serializer: every NEW emitter this epic adds (board card, ETag paths) inherits the envelope lane's nil-polarity verdict — field visibility fails closed, verified against both polarities.
  • In-flight collision: 56 taskboard files are dirty in the main checkout with uncommitted purpose/GetConditionalBounded work. The build wave starts from origin/main in a worktree and coordinates with that work's owner.

  6. Detail store bounds: infinite TTL governs validity, not disk — LRU byte cap (e.g. 32 MB) and own-directory vs snapshot-file cohabitation are open.
  7. Does the Studio board converge on the same wire card this epic freezes, or stay on server-side projection with a shared FIELD LIST only? (Cheapest honest option: shared field list now, shared wire later.)

Per-address granularity applies only to the detail cache, where the address (doc_id+rev) is exactly what an event carries.   • The board silently shows 32% of the corpus. 3,118 tasks live; the list clamps at 1,000 (parse_limit(…,1000,1000)). Un-truncation is the headline UX win, not the byte diet.
  • Everything the split needs already exists, unassembled. The /v1/tasks/events feed carries {id, event, doc_id, rev, at} with a replay-safe cursor — and has ZERO Go consumers. ETag machinery exists server-side (QueryController) and client-side (GetConditional) — and no task endpoint emits one; the only real-ETag caller in Go is the capabilities manifest. Rev is already the write path's CAS token (close observed_rev, 409 doc_changed_since_claim).
  • Studio already ships the pattern. board_live.ex projects compact cards server-side and does a FRESH per-task doc read for the peek pane (assign_peek) — the two-level split is live precedent, bespoke and inline, not greenfield theory. The epic formalizes what Studio improvised.
  • Brief v2 cannot serve the board as-is — eight missing fields (census above), two merge-hostile cuts, and no rev anywhere: not on the brief card, not in search brief cards, not even DECODED by the TUI (taskWire has no rev field although full view sends it — the client throws the handle away today).
  • Pulse churns rev every lease renewal while touching nothing any board projects — so invalidation classes by event kind are load-bearing, and task.criterion proves the classes don't align with board-vs-detail field boundaries (it lives in a detail key but moves the board's met/total).
  • AXI deliberately left the taskboard on full view ('hardcoded URLs, no view param — proven safe') and reserved task.get as the views-free escape hatch. This epic is the successor customer that work anticipated. Adjacent census gift for the view-tiers lane: agents typed the nonexistent bp task show 2,428 times (~1 MB of pure error waste) — an alias/hint is cheaper than any view optimization.

The write-path event spine (drives the invalidation classes)

Every task verb bumps doc.rev via CAS and emits exactly one primary event kind — except bare edge writes: Edges.add_dep touches only the task_edges table (no rev, NO event), while the Fence wrapper the facade routes through emits task.mutated only when it fences an in_progress dependent. Verbs → kinds: claim/renew→task.claimed, pulse→task.pulse, close→task.closed (+criterion/mutated/landed_under_you), release→task.released, stamp→task.criterion, stage→task.staged, move→task.reparented (same-parent = no write, no event), relabel→task.relabeled, paper-ref→task.referenced, compactor→task.compacted/.compaction_restored, TTL sweeper→task.lease_expired/.engagement_lapsed. A dependency edge on a non-in_progress task is the one write invisible to the feed — the whole-board refetch covers it; a per-event board patcher would not. One more argument for keeping board-tier refetch whole.

The template chapter — how any surface applies the kit

This is the chapter the crown paper generalizes. Four pieces plus a discipline, in exactly these words (sibling lanes: same words or amend the crown):

  1. Tier — a manifest-declared view per surface: the list card carries what the surface PAINTS (states, counts, flags), never what it might read. Fieldful nouns get field-projection views; blobful nouns (papers, sheets) get windows/handles instead — the fieldful-vs-blobful boundary is view-tiers-seam's law.
  2. Handle — doc_id + rev on every card, no exceptions. The handle IS the address, the cache key, and the CAS token. Bare rev always means document-CAS 32-hex.
  3. Cache — content-addressed by rev, TTL infinite. The store is the CMS; there is no second store to wipe, drift, or expire.
  4. Invalidation — a keyset feed of addresses, classed by event kind. Never TTL, never wall-clock, never 'once at session start'.
  5. Honesty — staleness is badged, never silent; emptiness is tri-state; degraded paths are authored, not accidental.

Risks & unknowns

The design renegotiates frozen contracts — say so, never slip it D13/D28 ('zero extra fetches — the wire already carries everything') and D12 ('preview NEVER fetches') are amendment-era FROZEN charter contracts that celebrate exactly what this design dismantles. The epic charter must open with explicit unfreezing language and the evidence that earned it (9.14 MB, 32% truncation). A build wave that quietly contradicts them repeats the false-done class of failure.
  • Drift honesty debt: today's board is drift-free by construction (refetch everything). Each cache layer added must prove its own honesty — badge visible, cursor validated, out-of-order fenced — as acceptance criteria with mutation-proven tests, not vibes.
  • Merge hazard if board rides brief unmodified: the seconds/claim cuts are not cosmetic; shipping the board on brief v2 as-is can strand stale claimed rows. Block on the card fix, not on hope.
  • Fail-closed serializer: every NEW emitter this epic adds (board card, ETag paths) inherits the envelope lane's nil-polarity verdict — field visibility fails closed, verified against both polarities.
  • In-flight collision: 56 taskboard files are dirty in the main checkout with uncommitted purpose/GetConditionalBounded work. The build wave starts from origin/main in a worktree and coordinates with that work's owner.
  • Events-feed scale: append-only forever is the correctness win; the covering-index optimization events.ex's own comment defers ('before the table 10×'s') becomes real once every board consumes the feed.

Judgment calls left open — for the user / epic strategist

  1. View naming ruling: grow views.supported to [brief, board, full] (this paper's recommendation) or ship board needs as brief v3? No standing rule decides; the charter must.
  2. Rev-on-card convergence: this lane, handle-doctrine, and view-tiers must land ONE proposal (recommended here: rev on every card of every view). If the crown rules otherwise, this design falls back to events-feed-only staleness with a full-refetch backstop — workable, blinder per card.
  3. Clamp: raise the board list to the full 3,118 (restoring truth, ~1.2 MB) or server-window with badged truncation? Interacts with folding — 2,238 of 3,118 are terminal (done/cancelled).
  4. Pulse class: is a rev-mismatched-but-badged cached detail acceptable for task.pulse (this paper says yes — the board row carries the fresh now)? Cheap to flip either way.
  5. Prefetch budget: cursor±2 and cap 4 are engineering judgment, not measurement — tune against real focus-latency once built; decide then whether ?ids= earns server work.
  6. Detail store bounds: infinite TTL governs validity, not disk — LRU byte cap (e.g. 32 MB) and own-directory vs snapshot-file cohabitation are open.
  7. Does the Studio board converge on the same wire card this epic freezes, or stay on server-side projection with a shared FIELD LIST only? (Cheapest honest option: shared field list now, shared wire later.)
